significance: A twelfth-century temple attributed to the Reddi kings, standing on the Devakuta hill on an islet in the Godavari and counted in the Skanda Purana among the five Kasi kshetras.
story: After Sati burned herself at Daksha's sacrifice, Shiva is said to have brought forth Veerabhadra and Bhadrakali; Veerabhadra beheaded Daksha and danced the Rudra Tandava here until sage Agastya calmed him and Shiva settled as a linga at the spot.
